message.content:
You are a COMPLETENESS reader in a verification cycle (Q-61). You work from the PRIMARY TRANSCRIPT ONLY — you must NOT read the write-up you are auditing (the DNA evidence file), so that what you list is independent of it. Your final text is raw data for an orchestrator. Do not edit any file.

PRIMARY ARTIFACT:
~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/prelim-hearing-transcripts/day2.txt
(~323k chars — a Rev machine transcript of Day 2 of the preliminary hearing in State of Utah v. Tyler James Robinson, Fourth District, Case 251403576.)

Optionally validate search method first: run `./tsearch.py --validate` from ~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research (quote the result) before relying on any search null.

SCOPE: the testimony of FBI DNA analyst BAKKER (roughly lines 5050–9640 — locate her testimony yourself and declare the exact line range you read; read it END TO END, not by keyword sampling) plus any other Day 2 passage where DNA results, DNA statistics, likelihood ratios, contributors, elimination samples, swabs, or lab communications are discussed (find them with case-insensitive greps for: DNA, likelihood, ratio, octillion, quintillion, contributor, swab, elimination, extract, consumed, allele, loci, mixture, STRmix — declare which patterns you ran and their hit counts).

TASK: produce the list of MATERIAL facts, caveats, limits, numbers, and null statements in this testimony that a library file titled "DNA evidence — what it can bear" MUST record to be a faithful account. For each item:
- id: C1-nn
- locator: day2.txt line number(s) + the Rev timestamp string on the turn
- content: the fact/caveat/limit, with a short verbatim quote (≤40 words)
- materiality: what a reader would get WRONG about what the DNA evidence can bear if this is omitted or misstated. If the honest answer is "nothing material," DROP the item — apply this gate strictly.

HAZARDS that bind you: (9) Rev's speaker labels are NOT evidence — witness answers carry counsel's names systematically; infer every speaker from content (question vs answer, argument vs ruling) and never resolve a label to a real person without a stated basis in adjacent content. (10) Timestamps are recording-stream locators; never convert to clock time. Keyword sampling finds topics and misses conclusions — that is why the Bakker range must be read end to end, with greps only as a supplement for the rest of the day.

LIVING-PERSONS RULES: Lance Twiggs was GRANTED use immunity by two offices; his sworn statement was received IN LIEU OF live testimony — nothing he said was tested by cross-examination; never phrase him as having "testified." Elimination-sample donors are NOT suspects — carry the record's own non-suspect framing whenever you record elimination results. Tyler Robinson is presumed innocent and has not been bound over. No case-posture statements. Quote minimally.

Output: method declaration (ranges read end-to-end with first/last line quotes, greps run with hit counts), then the item list (expect 20–60 items).

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. content.text:
All greps and reads are complete. Here is the completeness-reader output for Q-61.

---

# C1 COMPLETENESS READ — day2.txt (Bakker DNA testimony + all other Day 2 DNA passages)

## Method declaration

**Search validation:** `./tsearch.py --validate` run from the project root → `✓ method validated — known positive /use pliers/ found in day4.txt` (quoted verbatim).

**File:** `~/Documents/Kirk Robinson Research/files - Court record/CR-ACQ-2026-07-27_court-record-artifacts/prelim-hearing-transcripts/day2.txt`, 9,640 lines total. Lines 9599–9640 are Rev blog boilerplate, not transcript.

**Ranges read END TO END (continuous Read calls, no sampling):** lines **4400–9640**. This covers:
- **Faumuina segment (State witness, DNA-chain + report reading): lines 4408–5069.** First substantive line read: 4408 "Please be seated. The court is now in session…"; the DNA content begins at 4412 "…we're going to call an FBI DNA analyst out of order."
- **Bakker testimony: lines 5073–9581.** First line: 5073 "Your Honor, out of order, the defense would be calling Amanda Bakker." Last line of her presence: 9577 "All right. Thank you, Ms. Baker. You may step down." (adjournment follows at 9597: "…we'll go ahead and be adjourned until tomorrow at 1:00 PM").

**Greps run (case-insensitive, whole file), hit counts:** DNA 127; likelihood 21; ratio 34; octillion 2; quintillion 2; contributor 64; swab 24; elimination 14; extract 3; consumed 3; allele 28; loci 7; mixture 24; STRmix 31. **Hits outside the read range (lines 1–4399):** only lines 764/768 ("realistic **likelihood** of prejudice" — camera-access argument, not DNA) and 4062 ("a **mixture** of lay and expert opinion" — re a different witness). All 14 "elimination" hits fall inside the Bakker range. **Conclusion: no Day 2 DNA discussion exists outside lines 4408–9597.**

**Speaker attribution (hazard 9):** all attributions below are inferred from content, not labels. Basis: the "Michael Burt" turns call Bakker "out of order, the defense would be calling" (5073) and argue defense reliability positions (6427, 7965) → defense counsel; the "Mr. McBride" turns say "The State calls Sergeant Jen Faumuina" (4412) and argue the probable-cause/1102(b)(4) standard for admission (6639, 7953) → prosecutor; "Ms. Bakker" turns are first-person FBI-lab work descriptions → the witness. Within this range, labels and content were consistent — witness answers carry "Ms. Bakker," not counsel's name — but every item below was checked against the question/answer content.

**Transcript-integrity notes:** (a) the Rev marker "PART 11 OF 14 ENDS" is **missing** (markers jump from PART 10 [06:14:04] at line 6972 to PART 12 [07:22:04] at line 8118); the span was read end to end and appears continuous apart from the announced recess (06:41:24 → 07:03:46, lines 7592–7599), but a splice loss cannot be excluded from the text alone. (b) Machine garbles observed and normalized in items below: "Baker"→Bakker, "tau"→towel (5850), "loci building"→Losee building (8438), "TPOC's"→TPOX (6179), "SDRs"→STRs (8570), "Fulger"/"Folger" variant spellings (5277/7617), "912"→9,12 (8158), "1416"→14,16 (8222), "79.3"→7,9.3 (8242).

**Timestamps** are quoted as Rev recording-stream locators only, never clock time.

---

## Item list

**C1-01** — lines 4412 (05:00:12 preview) and 5073 (05:14:18)
"we're going to call an FBI DNA analyst out of order. It's a defense witness" / "out of order, the defense would be calling Amanda Bakker."
The FBI DNA analyst was a **defense** witness; her direct examination was by defense counsel and the State cross-examined. Materiality: a reader would otherwise assume the DNA analyst was a prosecution witness presenting the State's case in chief; the adversarial posture of every question below inverts.

**C1-02** — lines 4512–4556 (05:02:19–05:02:55), 4620–4660 (05:04:02–05:04:48)
Screwdriver collected from the rooftop by "the Utah Bureau of Forensic Services Crime Scene Response Team"; FBI took custody that evening; "The gun was packaged… provided to the ATF lab"; towel and screwdriver to the FBI lab.
Materiality: chain of custody and the split of testing (rifle→ATF, towel/screwdriver→FBI DNA) is the foundation for what the FBI DNA report can and cannot cover — notably, this DNA testimony does not report a rifle-surface DNA result.

**C1-03** — lines 4580–4612 (05:03:16–05:03:50)
"a long gun that was wrapped in a dark-colored towel… a Mauser 98 rifle… It was a bolt action," found in "a wooded area that's northeast of campus."
Materiality: fixes what Item 7 physically wrapped and where it was recovered; the towel — not the rifle — is the item carrying the headline DNA number.

**C1-04** — lines 4684–4777 (05:05:50–05:07:53)
State's Exhibit 31 is "the FBI report… that documents DNA testing," signed by Amanda Bakker; admitted over a **standing objection** ("No additional objections… I'll note the standing objection").
Materiality: the DNA results entered as a hearsay report under a preserved defense objection; omitting this misstates the contested status of the exhibit.

**C1-05** — lines 4797, 4821 (05:08:38, 05:08:58)
"Item 7, Towel from around Mauser or rifle, Serial Number 8863." / "Item 8, Screwdriver from perch."
Materiality: the item-number-to-object mapping; every statistic below is meaningless or mis-attachable without it.

**C1-06** — line 4877 (05:10:57)
"Male DNA was obtained from Item 7, sub 1… interpreted as originating from two individuals, one of whom is Twiggs. The DNA results… are 1.7 octillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors."
Materiality: the towel LR. Crucially, **both hypotheses condition on Twiggs** — the number compares (Twiggs+Robinson) vs (Twiggs+unknown). A file that renders this as "Robinson's DNA to a 1.7-octillion certainty" misstates what the statistic bears. (Transcript garble in this turn: "and what are 1.7 octillion".)

**C1-07** — lines 4901–4913 (05:11:34–05:11:41)
Item 8, sub 1 (swabs of the screwdriver **handle area**): "30 quintillion times more likely if Twiggs and T. Robinson are contributors, than if Twiggs and an unknown, unrelated person are contributors."
Materiality: the screwdriver LR, same conditional structure; also fixes that the swabbed area was the handle.

**C1-08** — lines 4933–4981 (05:12:12–05:12:56)
"Twiggs is Lance Twiggs. He was a roommate of Mr. Tyler Robinson"; both Twiggs's and Robinson's reference DNA obtained by buccal swab by law enforcement.
Materiality: identifies the comparison references and their collection method. (Carry the record's framing: Twiggs appears here as a roommate/reference-sample donor, not a suspect; and note he did not testify at this hearing — nothing here was his sworn account.)

**C1-09** — lines 4993–5045, 9585–9597 (05:13:04 ff.; 08:14:48 ff.)
Defense reserved cross of Faumuina "until she has completed her testimony"; the court adjourned Day 2 right after Bakker without Faumuina resuming.
Materiality: as of end of Day 2, the DNA chain-of-custody witness had **not** been crossed; her account was untested at this point in the record.

**C1-10** — lines 5141–5165, 8886–8906 (05:15:38–05:16:29; 07:50:21–07:51:24)
Bakker: "forensic examiner in the DNA Casework Unit of the FBI laboratory… Quantico" — 10+ years as examiner (since 2015), ~6 years before that as biologist; B.S. biology.
Materiality: the qualification basis for every opinion; also the fact she manages the case and reviews data — the wet-lab work is done by others (see C1-24).

**C1-11** — lines 5189–5213 (05:16:48–05:17:34)
Evidence first received "September 11th of 2025"; case worked at "Priority 1 Level… 24 hours a day, seven days a week"; "conducting the analysis as the evidence was being inventoried"; normal turnaround "on average… between 180 and 200 days."
Materiality: the compressed, out-of-normal-sequence timeline (days instead of months, testing during intake) is a condition on the reliability discussion; omitting it hides both the speed and the deviation from routine workflow.

**C1-12** — line 5277 (05:19:02)
Sept 13, 2025 communication-log entry: "Spoke with FBI Special Agent Folger and Utah SBI SA Dave Hull. Gave technically reviewed results that Robinson was included as a **possible contributor** to the DNA from the towel and the screwdriver."
Materiality: the earliest reported conclusion, its exact hedged wording ("possible contributor"), and that results were relayed to investigators two days before the written report (report dated Sept 15, line 5321, 05:20:44).

**C1-13** — lines 5529–5549 (05:25:15–05:25:48)
FBI/DOJ standard: "an examiner may not state or imply that a match provides an absolute identification"; Bakker: "You never said it was an absolute identification of Mr. Robinson, did you?" — "Correct. No, I did not."
Materiality: the ceiling on what the DNA evidence can bear, conceded by the analyst herself.

**C1-14** — lines 5553–5597 (05:25:49–05:27:08)
Same standard: no "reasonable degree of scientific certainty" language; "An examiner may not state or imply that forensic autosomal DNA examinations have a zero error rate or are infallible" — Bakker followed both.
Materiality: bars the two strongest rhetorical framings a summary file might otherwise import.

**C1-15** — lines 5617–5633 (05:27:16–05:27:44)
Sources of error: "Human error could be an error… One of the big things is potential human error… also… how items are collected or how those items are tested."
Materiality: the analyst's own stated error model; a file claiming DNA testing is error-free would contradict the witness.

**C1-16** — lines 5710–5730 (05:29:25–05:30:29)
DOJ policy: "An examiner shall not assert that a likelihood ratio of any magnitude provides an absolute identification or source attribution" — "You're not implying that those numbers… provides an absolute identification of Mr. Robinson or Mr. Twiggs?" "No, I'm not."
Materiality: directly caps the meaning of the octillion/quintillion figures; the single most-needed caveat next to C1-06/07.

**C1-17** — lines 5750–5786 (05:30:45–05:32:18)
Activity level: "I cannot give an opinion as far as activity level goes… just because DNA is on an item doesn't necessarily mean that an individual touched it or utilized that item"; and she cannot say **when** DNA was deposited.
Materiality: the DNA results cannot, by the analyst's own policy and testimony, establish handling or timing — the two inferences a reader is most tempted to draw.

**C1-18** — lines 5794–5798, 9160–9163 (05:32:33–05:32:46; 08:01:11)
DNA persists "rather indefinitely" under ideal conditions ("items… 40 and 50 years old" have yielded DNA); DNA can arrive "via direct contact… body fluids… or through transfer" to an object the person never touched.
Materiality: persistence plus secondary transfer together define the outer bounds of innocent-deposit explanations the record itself allows.

**C1-19** — lines 5846–5850 (05:34:11 turn)
Degradation observed: Item 8 (screwdriver) "some degradation… a ski slope-type effect"; Item 7 (towel, garbled "tau") "slight amount of degradation, but not as much as Item 8."
Materiality: sample-condition facts; also the pegs for the State's later point (C1-45) that degradation did not affect conclusions.

**C1-20** — lines 5942–5958, 5966 (05:37:48–05:38:12; 05:38:24)
Method: GlobalFiler kit, "21 different locations… in addition to three sex determining locations"; STR testing measures **length only** — "not measuring the sequence within the boxcars."
Materiality: defines exactly what was measured; the sequence blind spot returns as the isoallele point (C1-41).

**C1-21** — lines 6043–6055, 6079–6087 (05:40:26–05:41:12; 05:41:59)
"For item seven, I did develop a full profile." / "Item eight was a partial profile, so I did not develop DNA at every single location… I did not have data at all 23 locations to compare."
Materiality: the towel and screwdriver results are not evidentially equal — the 30-quintillion figure rests on a partial profile with untestable loci.

**C1-22** — lines 6179–6199 (05:44:25–05:44:43)
At TPOX (garbled "TPOC's"), Robinson is 8,9 and Twiggs 8,11, but sample 8A "didn't have any of those types… so I could not compare at that location."
Materiality: concrete instance of missing loci in the screwdriver sample; shows the comparison is over fewer markers than the kit provides.

**C1-23** — lines 6343–6347, 6531–6535, 6699 (05:47:06 ff.; 05:53:30; 05:59:04)
Both Items 7 and 8 were **mixtures**; challenge rises with many contributors at similar levels; "in this case it was also only a mixture of two individuals."
Materiality: the two-person character of the mixtures is Bakker's stated answer to the PCAST criticism (C1-26); dropping either side distorts the dispute.

**C1-24** — lines 6543, 7012–7020 (05:53:41; 06:14:52–06:15:06)
"I did not calculate that personally. Part of the STRmix software… uses math and biological modeling to try to break that mixture into its individual contributors" and computes the LR; other analysts perform testing steps, feeding a case file she relies on.
Materiality: the statistics are software outputs on a division of labor, not a single analyst's hand computation — relevant to what "her" conclusion consists of.

**C1-25** — lines 6547–6559 (05:54:09–05:54:50)
